text:
There’s been a shot on target now, and it’s only gone in! It’s from a corner – one of those where the defender ushers the ball out of play thinking he’s about to get a goal-kick only for the fourth official to point to the corner – from which Yilmaz heads goalwards, the ball loops up off Jackson, and Deniz Gul heads it in! Not only that, just after he does so he gets volleyed in the face by Nicolas Jackson, who was a bit late in trying to clear the ball.
The two early kick-offs are now into their 75th minute, and still none of the four teams have had a shot on target. Galatasaray and Aston Villa are currently drawing 2-2 on shots off target and 0-0 on actual goals, while Bodo/Glimt and Lask are drawing 3-3 on shots off target and 0-0 on actual goals.
Team news has landed for the 8pm games, and here are the lineups for the two involving English teams:
Arsenal v Borussia Dortmund
Arsenal: Arrizabalaga, White, Konsa, Gabriel, Hincapie, Lewis-Skelly, Rice, Madueke, Odegaard, Tzolis, Gyokeres. Subs: Meslier, Saliba, Mosquera, Eze, Timber, Merino, Havertz, Calafiori, Guimaraes, Dowman, Porter.
Borussia Dortmund: Kobel, Gadou, Anton, Schlotterbeck, Ryerson, Nmecha, Veerman, Svensson, Bellingham, Beier, Silva. Subs: Drewes, Meyer, Bensebaini, Guirassy, Chukwuemeka, Nwaneri, Karetsas, Sabitzer, Mane, Albert, Duarte, Reggiani.
Referee: Maurizio Mariani (Italy).
Man City v Napoli
Man City: Donnarumma, Matheus Luiz, Gvardiol, Guehi, O’Reilly, Anderson, Bouaddi, Allan, Cherki, Fernandez, Haaland. Subs: Rulli, Dias, Ndiaye, Kovacic, Doku, Ait Nouri, Vitor Reis, Khusanov, Foden, McAidoo, Floyd Samba, Lewis.
Napoli: Milinkovic-Savic, Beukema, Rrahmani, Olivera, Politano, De Bruyne, Gilmour, McTominay, Spinazzola, Lang, Hojlund. Subs: Contini, Spinelli, Neres, Lucca, Giovane, Chiummariello, Anguissa.
Referee: Istvan Kovacs (Romania).
An absolutely terrible, cynical challenge from Joao Gomes earns him a yellow card and so riles his victim, Yunus Akgun, that he ends up with one two, which is a bit rum.
Handbags in Istanbul! Tackles go flying in, players square up to each other, and at the end of it all both Aleksei Batrakov and John McGinn find their names in the referee’s book. It was a bodycheck from McGinn, to which Batrakov responded by kicking out a leg and confronting the Scot. And all of that followed a fair but full-blooded tackle by Sanchez on Alysson, which while being fine was only the finest of margins away from being outrageous.
In the meantime, here’s Will Unwin looking ahead to Manchester City v Napoli:
As Manchester City come to terms with turbulence, one of their all-time greats has flown in to remind them of the best of times. Kevin De Bruyne will be back at the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday, evoking the greatest period of Pep Guardiola’s decade in charge when they won four straight Premier League titles and the Champions League.
In Europe, things are comfortable for Enzo Maresca, with three wins from four, but they have collected a solitary point from 12 domestically recently. They are struggling to score and conceding too easily at the back, leading the Italian to experiment in his attempts to find solutions.
De Bruyne left for nothing in the summer of 2025, but had fully returned the £55m City paid for him 10 years previously. Six Premier League titles, two FA Cups, five League Cups, a Club World Cup and that night in Istanbul when City conquered Inter, successes he will for ever cherish.
The two early kick-offs have just reached half-time, and they have featured a combined total of not a single shot on target. There have also been no own-goals, and thus the scores on the doors are:
Hello world! There’s a lot going on tonight, with eight Championship fixtures, four in League One, a couple in League Two and three in the Scottish Premiership, all of which, as is traditional, we will largely ignore unless something extraordinary happens. That’s because there’s more than enough enough going on in Europe to keep us occupied, with particular focus on Kevin de Bruyne’s return to the Etihad Stadium with Napoli. The Belgian is something of a lapsed assist machine these days, having laid on just two goals so far this season, and not a single one in Serie A since the Neopolitans’ 2-0 win at Genoa on the opening day, but he remains Kevin de Bryne and we will be treated with appropriate reverence. He ‘s certainly been saying the right things pre-match: “I have nothing but affection for this club and that will never change,” he gushed. “I’m proud of what I’ve done as a football player and, honestly, this is my club.”
